newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria plans 4.0 mln tonne phosphate output by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Syria plans 4.0 mln tonne phosphate output by 2000.

text.p: Syria plans to increase its yearly phosphate production by 56 percent within three years, the general director of the state-owned establishment for phosphate and mines said on Thursday.
Adnan al-Ahmad told Reuters Syria wants to increase output to around four million tonnes by the year 2000 from an expected 2.6 million this year, and around 2.1 million tonnes in 1996.
He said the increase would be achieved through modernisation of equipment and the introduction of new methods to wash phosphate.

"Syrian phosphate has a low percentage of heavy components, which makes it good for the environment and also makes Europeans want to buy it. When it (phosphate) is washed, as well, it will find a better market," al-Ahmad said.
He said Syria has exported around 817,000 tonnes to European countries so far this year, and sold about 208,000 tonnes to the state-owned fertilizers establishment.
Total production in first-half 1997 was around 1.2 million tonnes, and plans are under way to meet the 2.6 million tonne target, he said.
